title: Minimum Cost to Connect Sticks
summary: Given an array of stick lengths, find the minimum cost to connect all sticks into one by repeatedly joining two sticks at a time, where the cost of joining is the sum of their lengths.
statement: Given an array of stick lengths, find the minimum cost to connect all sticks into one by repeatedly joining two sticks at a time, where the cost of joining is the sum of their lengths.
constraints: Every merge costs the sum of its two sticks.
hints: A min-heap exposes the two shortest current sticks.
Merge those two, add their length to cost, and push the combined stick back.
The exchange argument for optimal merge patterns shows the two least weights can be siblings in an optimal tree.
editorial: The exchange argument for optimal merge patterns shows the two least weights can be siblings in an optimal tree.

tests.explanation: Merge two and three for five, then five and four for nine: total fourteen.
Repeatedly merging the two shortest gives total thirty.
